brief.headline: Friday's missing exchange price has now been published and it confirms what the off-market evidence already said - aluminium fell about two percent to $3,274 a tonne, along with every other metal on the board, on American inflation data rather than on anything to do with aluminium itself; the tightness for metal available right now did not budge.
bullets: WHAT HAPPENED. The exchange price that was missing yesterday has now appeared, and it was down. Aluminium settled at $3,274 a tonne, $69 lower than Thursday, a fall of about two percent and the biggest one-day drop since prices started climbing at the beginning of September. Stocks in exchange warehouses edged down again, by 250 tonnes.

WHY IT IS NOT AN ALUMINIUM STORY. Every metal on the board fell on the same day - zinc, nickel and aluminium all around two percent, copper about one percent, lead barely at all. When everything moves together like that, the cause is almost always something outside the metals themselves. Here it was American inflation figures released that afternoon: the core rate came in a tenth of a point higher than forecast, which pushed traders towards expecting an interest-rate RISE at the US central bank meeting on 16 September. The dollar strengthened, and a stronger dollar makes every dollar-priced metal more expensive for buyers elsewhere.

THE PART THAT DID NOT MOVE, AND WHY IT MATTERS MOST. Metal for immediate delivery still costs MORE than metal for delivery in three months - a $24 premium, versus $25 the day before. That gap barely changed even as the headline price dropped two percent. If the fall had been caused by customers not wanting metal, that premium would have collapsed. It did not. So the paper market repriced and the physical market did not follow - the two are pointing in opposite directions, which is worth watching rather than smoothing over.

A NOTE ON THE NUMBERS THEMSELVES. Yesterday this page refused to move the price forward because the exchange had not published it, and instead showed two other public marks suggesting the market had fallen to about $3,246-3,274. The official figure has now landed within about three dollars of those marks. That is worth saying plainly: waiting for the real number rather than carrying an old one forward turned out to be the right call.

WHAT TO WATCH NEXT. The US central bank decides on 16 September and that is now the biggest scheduled event in front of this market. Also watch whether the premium for immediate metal keeps holding up if prices fall further - that is the clearest test of whether physical demand is genuinely intact or just slow to react. And note one side-effect of a lower exchange price: because the US import tariff is charged as a percentage, a cheaper benchmark means a smaller tariff bill but a WIDER underlying market premium.

kpis.label: LME Cash settlement
kpis.note: THE FRIDAY 11-SEPTEMBER LME BOARD HAS NOW BEEN PUBLISHED AND THIS PAGE HAS ADVANCED ONTO IT. The prior compile carried the 10-September official because Friday's metals and warehouse board genuinely had not been posted; it has since appeared on Westmetall's GERMAN overview, requested with a cache-busting query string, and it is corroborated line for line by the aluminium, copper and zinc per-metal daily tables. THE ENGLISH OVERVIEW IS NOW THE STALE PAGE - it still shows 10-September - which is the exact MIRROR IMAGE of the 04-August incident, when English led and German lagged. NEITHER LANGUAGE VERSION CAN BE TRUSTED ALONE; the newer of the two, confirmed against the per-metal tables, is what is published here. THE SESSION ITSELF WAS BROADLY LOWER AND ALUMINIUM WAS IN THE MIDDLE OF IT, NOT THE CAUSE OF IT. Cash settled at $3,274.00, DOWN $69.00 or 2.06% from the $3,343.00 struck on 10-September, and it is the largest single-session fall since the board turned up in early September. THE MOST IMPORTANT THING TO SAY ABOUT THIS NUMBER IS THAT IT WAS FORESEEN AND IS NOT A SURPRISE. The previous compile declined to advance the board but published two dated off-exchange marks and stated plainly that both sat BELOW the carried official: SMM's record of the 10-September futures close at $3,274.50 and a Trading Economics reference for 11-September at $3,246.95. THE PUBLISHED OFFICIAL HAS LANDED ALMOST EXACTLY ON THEM - cash $3,274.00 against that $3,274.50 futures close, a difference of FIFTY CENTS, and three-month $3,250.00 against that $3,246.95 reference, a difference of $3.05. That is a clean after-the-fact validation of refusing to carry a stale number as if it were current, and it is recorded here because the discipline earned its keep rather than because it flattered the page. The month-to-date cash average is $3,301.78 across nine September sessions and the prior-month benchmark average of $3,249.62 is the August cash mean over twenty sessions, recomputed from the per-metal daily table this run.

kpis.label: LME 3-month
kpis.note: Three-month officials settled at $3,250.00, DOWN $68.00 or 2.05% on the day, moving essentially in lockstep with cash - the front fell $69.00 and the back $68.00. THAT NEAR-IDENTICAL MOVE IS ITSELF THE SIGNAL AND IT POINTS AWAY FROM ALUMINIUM. A curve that shifts down in parallel is being repriced by something OUTSIDE the metal - the discount rate and the dollar - rather than by a change in the availability of near-dated units, which would have moved the front and the back by different amounts. EVERY METAL ON THE BOARD FELL ON THE SAME SESSION, which is the corroborating evidence: on three-month officials zinc was worst at -2.27%, then nickel -2.06%, aluminium -2.05%, copper -0.96% and lead -0.29%. ALUMINIUM WAS NOT SINGLED OUT; it sat in the middle of a complex-wide move. The comparison figure of $3,251.22 is the August three-month average.

kpis.label: Cash-3M spread
kpis.note: The cash-to-three-month spread is a BACKWARDATION of $24.00, cash above three-month, essentially unchanged from the $25.00 backwardation of 10-September - it narrowed by a single dollar. THIS IS THE MOST INFORMATIVE ROW ON THE BOARD TODAY PRECISELY BECAUSE IT DID ALMOST NOTHING. Flat price fell 2.06% while the structure held, and a backwardation that survives a two-percent sell-off is saying that the people who need metal NOW still need it now. A macro-driven sell-off tends to leave the physical structure intact; a demand-driven one usually collapses the front. THIS ONE DID NOT COLLAPSE THE FRONT. SPREAD AND FLAT PRICE ARE THEREFORE POINTING IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS AND THAT DIVERGENCE IS FLAGGED DELIBERATELY: the paper market repriced and the physical market did not follow it. The prior-period average of -$1.60 is a CONTANGO, so the market remains structurally tighter than its own recent history by roughly $26.

kpis.label: LME stocks (t)
kpis.note: Exchange stocks fell 250 tonnes to 244,100 - a rounding error on a 244,000-tonne base, and the fifth consecutive small draw. THE POINT IS NOT THE SIZE OF THE DRAW BUT THAT IT WAS A DRAW AT ALL ON A DAY THE PRICE FELL TWO PERCENT. Warehouses did not receive metal on a sharply lower price, which is consistent with the backwardation holding and inconsistent with a genuine demand-led break. Stocks remain roughly 7,100 tonnes below the prior-period average of 251,215 and about 265,000 tonnes below the January peak above 509,000.

kpis.label: EUR/USD (LME FX fixing)
kpis.note: The LME FX fixing is $1.15920 per euro against $1.16170, a DOLLAR STRENGTHENING of about 0.22% - and unlike the metals rows this one was already published and carried on the prior run, because Westmetall had posted Friday's currency section while withholding the metals board. THE SEQUENCE NOW READS CLEANLY IN ONE DIRECTION: American August consumer prices printed a core rate a tenth above forecast on 11-September, the dollar firmed into the settlement, and every dollar-denominated metal on the board fell. A stronger dollar mechanically raises the local-currency cost of the same tonne for every buyer outside the dollar bloc, which is the transmission channel from a US inflation print to a London aluminium price. The fixing sits marginally above the $1.1585 comparison average, so this is a day-move rather than a regime change.

lme.commentary:

THE SESSION. Cash settled $3,274.00, down $69.00 or 2.06%. Three-month settled $3,250.00, down $68.00 or 2.05%. Stocks drew 250 tonnes to 244,100. The cash-to-three-month backwardation is $24.00 against $25.00 - a ONE-DOLLAR narrowing on a session in which flat price fell more than two percent. 

WHAT THE CURVE SAYS. Cash and three-month fell by $69.00 and $68.00 - a parallel shift, not a twist. A parallel shift is the signature of a curve being repriced by the discount rate and the currency, not by a change in the availability of near-dated metal, which would necessarily have moved the two legs by different amounts. The corroboration is that EVERY METAL ON THE BOARD FELL ON THE SAME SESSION: on three-month officials zinc -2.27%, nickel -2.06%, aluminium -2.05%, copper -0.96%, lead -0.29%. ALUMINIUM WAS NOT SINGLED OUT AND WAS NOT THE WORST ROW. 

SPREAD AND FLAT PRICE DIVERGED AND THAT IS FLAGGED DELIBERATELY. Flat price fell 2.06% while the backwardation held within a dollar and stocks drew rather than built. A demand-led break flattens or flips the front of the curve and pushes metal back into warehouses. NEITHER HAPPENED. The physical market did not ratify the paper move. That divergence is the single most decision-relevant observation on the board today and it argues the sell-off was financial in origin. 

THE CAUSE, DATED. US August consumer prices were released on 11-September. Headline 3.4% year on year and +0.4% month on month, both in line; core 2.4% year on year, easing and in line; but CORE +0.3% ON THE MONTH, A TENTH ABOVE FORECAST. Reporting describes traders raising the odds of a Federal Reserve RISE at the 16-September decision. The LME FX fixing moved to $1.15920 per euro from $1.16170, a dollar strengthening of about 0.22% into the settlement. The chain from the print to the price is short and it is dated at every link. 

A VALIDATION WORTH RECORDING. The prior compile declined to advance the board and instead published two dated off-exchange marks, stating that the carried official was both stale AND high: an SMM record of the 10-September futures close at $3,274.50 and a Trading Economics reference for 11-September at $3,246.95. THE PUBLISHED OFFICIALS LANDED AT CASH $3,274.00 AND THREE-MONTH $3,250.00 - fifty cents from the first mark and $3.05 from the second. Refusing to carry a stale number forward as though it were current, and publishing the uncertainty instead, produced the correct read a day early.

drivers.text: THE PENDING ASIAN QUARTERLY RANGE IS UNCHANGED AT $280-310 BECAUSE NO NEW DATED INPUT PRINTED, AND THE RULE THAT KEPT IT UNCHANGED IS THE SAME RULE THAT MOVED IT ON FRIDAY — This page narrowed the pending Q4 Japanese range from $290-325 to $280-310 on 11-September, the first change in nine runs, and it did so only when a dated public consensus finally printed. TODAY NOTHING NEW PRINTED AND THE RANGE THEREFORE DOES NOT MOVE - a range is not tightened on a second reading of the same evidence. The lower bound remains the floor of the SMM market consensus of USD 280-290/t reported 11-September, with Korean and Thai traders described as already repricing toward that band. The upper bound remains the FLOOR of the $310-325/t producer offer for October-December shipments reported 02-September against the settled Q3 record of $395. BOTH ENDS ARE QUOTED NUMBERS FROM DATED 2026 SOURCES AND NEITHER IS AN ESTIMATE. The significance is unchanged and it is directional rather than arithmetic: the consensus sits BELOW the level at which producers opened, so the burden of concession is on the sellers.
drivers.source: Shanghai Metals Market (SMM), 11-September-2026 - market consensus for the upcoming MJP settlement at USD 280-290/t; Korean and Thai traders repricing toward that band

drivers.text: THE GULF-SCARCITY PILLAR THAT SUPPORTS EVERY WESTERN PREMIUM ON THIS PANEL WAS CONTRADICTED AGAIN, BY THE SAME SOURCE THIS PAGE USES FOR ITS BULLISH CHINESE DATA — SMM's 11-September market review states that outside China, production resumptions and new capacity ramp-ups continued, that DAMAGED CAPACITY IN THE MIDDLE EAST RECOVERED, and that aluminium supply outside China kept repairing. It is the second independent statement in the same week from that source pointing the same way, the first being that Middle Eastern and Australian ingot supply into Japan is relatively ample. THAT SITS DIRECTLY AGAINST PUBLICLY DISCLOSED CAPACITY STILL OUT - Qatalum at roughly 60% of a 648,000-tonne nameplate on reduced gas with a force majeure outstanding and no resolution date, Alba's reduction lines 1-3 idled since March 2026, and GCC primary output down 44% year on year in July. BOTH ARE PUBLIC AND DATED AND THE PAGE DOES NOT FORCE THEM TO AGREE. The reconciliation that fits both is that Gulf OUTPUT is genuinely lower while Gulf METAL is nonetheless reaching Asia in quantity, which makes the tightness locational rather than absolute - and locational premia decay faster than deficits.
drivers.source: Shanghai Metals Market (SMM) morning review, 11-September-2026 - 'damaged capacity in the Middle East recovered, and aluminium supply outside China kept repairing'

drivers.text: THE ONE PREMIUM THAT ROSE THIS WEEK WAS CHINESE AND DOMESTIC, AND THE REASON IS A STRUCTURAL DIVERSION OF METAL BEFORE IT EVER BECOMES A TRADABLE INGOT — A Mysteel review dated 11-September reports the SOUTH CHINA A00 INGOT BASIS AT A YEAR-TO-DATE HIGH while East China and Central Plains basis levels stayed broadly stable - a regional divergence with an explicit inventory arithmetic behind it. Foshan trader inventory was 144,000 tonnes at 03-September; stripping roughly 37,000 tonnes of unclear ownership leaves about 107,000 tonnes actually held; and after warrants degraded by prolonged-storage steel-strap corrosion and Russian units locked into term contracts for direct delivery to end-users, FREELY TRADABLE INVENTORY IS ESTIMATED AT ONLY ABOUT 50,000 TONNES. THE CAUSE IS MOLTEN-METAL DIVERSION AND IT IS QUANTIFIED: Yunnan and Guangxi are commissioning at least 760,000 tonnes of annualised molten-aluminium conversion capacity in 2026, roughly 550,000 tonnes of it Yunnan slab - over 70% of the increment - pulled by battery-foil and electronic-foil processing margins, while north-to-south capacity transfer has fallen short of expectations. THE LIMIT IS STATED: this is a Chinese domestic basis, not a Western delivered premium, and nothing has been written into any row on this panel on the strength of it.
drivers.source: Mysteel via AL Circle, 11-September-2026 - South China A00 basis at a year-to-date high; Foshan tradable inventory arithmetic; 760,000 t of new southwest molten-aluminium conversion capacity

drivers.text: THE US TARIFF DECOMPOSITION IS UNCHANGED THIS RUN FOR A MECHANICAL REASON, AND THE SENSITIVITY IT HIDES IS FLAGGED BEFORE IT BITES — Section 232 stands at 50% on articles and 25% on derivative articles, with Canada's 50% counter-tariffs in force since 08-September. THE DECOMPOSITION HAS MOVED THIS RUN BECAUSE THE BENCHMARK MOVED, AND IT MOVED AGAINST THE OBVIOUS INTUITION. At 50% on the newly published $3,274.00 cash benchmark the TARIFF LEG IS $1,637.00, down from $1,671.50 on the 10-September benchmark. With the US duty-paid assessment standing still at $2,094/t, the implied MARKET LEG WIDENS from $422.50 TO $457.00 - an increase of $34.50, or roughly 8%. THIS IS THE ASYMMETRY THIS PAGE FLAGGED IN ADVANCE ON THE PRIOR RUN AND IT HAS NOW MATERIALISED: at a 50% rate every $10 fall in the benchmark cuts the tariff leg by $5 and, with the assessment unchanged, mechanically WIDENS the implied market leg by $5. A FALLING EXCHANGE PRICE THEREFORE MAKES THE UNDERLYING US PHYSICAL PREMIUM LOOK STRONGER, NOT WEAKER, WITHOUT ANY PHYSICAL TIGHTENING HAVING OCCURRED. THE HONEST CAVEAT IS THAT THIS IS ARITHMETIC, NOT EVIDENCE OF DEMAND: the widening is an artefact of a percentage tariff applied to a lower base while a periodic assessment has not yet been re-struck. It should not be read as a US market tightening until a fresh duty-paid assessment prints against the new benchmark.
drivers.source: Trading Economics / public tariff schedule and US duty-paid assessment, decomposition recomputed on the 11-Sep-2026 LME cash benchmark

SMM reports that on 11-September-2026, 50,000 mt of alumina traded at $353.50/mt FOB EAST AUSTRALIA for October shipment. THE BASIS IS IDENTICAL TO THE MARK IT REPLACES, which is why it was accepted: the row previously carried $356/t from a 05-August trade on the same FOB East Australia basis. The move is DOWN $2.50, or 0.7%, over five weeks - a small decline, and the smallness is the finding. AFTER FIVE WEEKS OF CARRYING A STALE NUMBER AND FLAGGING AN EXPECTED DECLINE, THE MARKET DELIVERED ALMOST NO DECLINE AT ALL. SMM has been publicly guiding that the September monthly average alumina price would fall on surplus, high operating capacity and continued inventory buildup; the first hard print of the month is essentially flat. That is a modest but real disappointment to the falling-cost thesis. A SECOND DATED TRADE ON THE SAME DAY IS CARRIED FOR CONTEXT AND NOT MIXED INTO THIS ROW: 50,000 mt traded at $373/mt FOB INDONESIA for November-2026 shipment, a $19.50 premium to the Australian basis on a later shipment month. The 11-September metals and warehouse board appeared on Westmetall's GERMAN overview, requested with a cache-busting query string, and it is confirmed line for line by the aluminium, copper and zinc per-metal daily tables. ALUMINIUM FELL 2.06% ON THE PUBLISHED 11-SEPTEMBER SESSION - CASH $3,274.00, THREE-MONTH $3,250.00, STOCKS 244,100 TONNES - AND THE ENTIRE BASE-METALS BOARD FELL WITH IT. On three-month officials zinc -2.27%, nickel -2.06%, aluminium -2.05%, copper -0.96%, lead -0.29%. THE BREADTH IS THE POINT: a simultaneous fall across five metals is a macro repricing, not an aluminium story, and aluminium was not the weakest row. THE OFF-EXCHANGE MARKS PUBLISHED HERE YESTERDAY WERE VINDICATED - an SMM 10-September futures close of $3,274.50 and a Trading Economics 11-September reference of $3,246.95 bracketed officials that printed at $3,274.00 and $3,250.00. CRUCIALLY, THE BACKWARDATION HELD AT $24.00 AGAINST $25.00 AND STOCKS DREW AGAIN: price fell, tightness did not.

US AUGUST CONSUMER PRICES LANDED IN LINE ON THE HEADLINE AND HOT ON THE CORE MONTH, AND THE RATE MARKET MOVED FURTHER TOWARD A RISE. Headline CPI was 3.4% year on year and +0.4% month on month, both matching expectations after +0.1% in July, with gasoline up 3.9% and accounting for more than a third of the monthly increase. Core eased to 2.4% year on year from 2.5%, in line - but core rose 0.3% on the month, a tenth above forecast, and reporting on the release describes traders increasing the odds of a Federal Reserve RISE next week. The fed funds target has sat at 3.50-3.75% for all of 2026. This resolved the single highest-impact catalyst this page carried yesterday, and it resolved it against the metal.

THE ODDS THEMSELVES ARE NOW ON THE PAGE RATHER THAN DESCRIBED. CME FedWatch probabilities recorded in SMM's 11-September review: for SEPTEMBER, unchanged 28.8% and a cumulative 25 basis point HIKE 71.3%; for OCTOBER, unchanged 17.6%, cumulative 25bp 54.8% and cumulative 50bp 27.6%. August producer prices the day before printed 5.4% year on year against 5.3% expected, with core PPI +0.2% on the month against +0.3% expected - mixed in composition, hawkish in effect. SMM's own conclusion is that a stronger dollar is weighing on metals valuations and that aluminium futures inside and outside China are weakening in tandem.

CHINESE SOCIAL INVENTORY BROKE BELOW 800,000 TONNES AND THE MECHANISM BEHIND IT IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN SEASONAL. Stocks fell to 796,000 tonnes on 10-September. Weekly aluminium production held STEADY at 874,700 tonnes while the proportion of output leaving smelters as LIQUID aluminium rose 0.15 percentage points to 78.93%, which mechanically reduces the volume cast into ingot. Less ingot cast is less ingot available to warrant, inventory or ship, so inventory can fall without a single additional tonne being consumed. Leading downstream processors ran at about 61.3%, up slightly month on month, as the September peak season began.

THE SOUTH CHINA INGOT BASIS HIT A YEAR-TO-DATE HIGH AND THE INVENTORY ARITHMETIC BEHIND IT IS UNUSUALLY EXPLICIT. A Mysteel review dated 11-September puts Foshan trader inventory at 144,000 tonnes as of 03-September; stripping roughly 37,000 tonnes of unclear ownership leaves about 107,000 tonnes actually held; and after warrants degraded by prolonged-storage steel-strap corrosion and Russian units locked into term contracts for direct delivery, FREELY TRADABLE INVENTORY IS ESTIMATED AT ONLY ABOUT 50,000 TONNES. The cause is molten-metal diversion: Yunnan and Guangxi are commissioning at least 760,000 tonnes of annualised molten-aluminium conversion capacity in 2026, roughly 550,000 tonnes of it Yunnan slab - over 70% of the increment - pulled by battery-foil and electronic-foil processing margins, while the transfer of capacity from north to south has fallen short of expectations.

THE MOST DIRECT PUBLIC CONTRADICTION YET OF THE GULF-SCARCITY PILLAR, AND IT COMES FROM THE SAME SOURCE THIS PAGE USES FOR THE BULLISH CHINESE DATA. SMM's 11-September review states that outside China, production resumptions and new capacity ramp-ups continued, that DAMAGED CAPACITY IN THE MIDDLE EAST RECOVERED, and that aluminium supply outside China kept repairing. That sits directly against publicly disclosed Gulf capacity still out - Qatalum at roughly 60% of a 648,000-tonne nameplate on reduced gas with a second force majeure outstanding and no resolution date, and Alba's reduction lines 1, 2 and 3 idled since March 2026. Both statements are public and dated. The page does not force them to agree; it records that the direction of travel in the Gulf is now toward recovery on the only dated commentary available.

THE CHINESE SPOT TAPE WAS SOFT ON THE SAME DAY AS THE DESTOCK, AND BOTH HALVES ARE PRINTED. SMM A00 closed at RMB 24,560 per tonne, flat on the previous trading day. Ingot transactions cleared at a discount of RMB 30 to RMB 10 against the contract, with actual central China trades reported around a discount of RMB 150-180 to the September contract. Downstream processors bought small volumes on an as-needed basis at high absolute prices, traders showed no appetite at high levels, and SMM describes transaction feedback as poor with supply increasing and demand decreasing. ALUMINIUM BILLET INVENTORY CONTINUES TO BUILD, WHICH SMM FLAGS AS POTENTIAL PRESSURE FOR INVENTORY TO SHIFT BACK INTO INGOT - the mechanism that would unwind the ingot tightness described one headline above.

THE BACKWARDATION FINDING FROM THE PRIOR RUN IS FROZEN RATHER THAN CONFIRMED, AND ONE NEW FACT WEAKENS IT. The +$25.00 cash-over-three-month spread is the 10-September reading, the widest since 04-August and the fourth consecutive widening - and the first of the four in which the spread widened while the flat price fell. With no 11-September official there is no fifth session and the central test remains unanswered. The weakening fact is that the 10-September futures session CLOSED at $3,274.50, $43.50 below the three-month official from which that spread is computed, so the backwardation was struck at a settlement the day then repudiated. The curve-quality risk has been raised from DOWN to FLAT on that basis rather than left where a flattering reading would have put it.

THE SCRAP DISCOUNT WIDENED AGAIN, WHICH IS A QUIET INDICATOR OF PRIMARY TIGHTNESS AND OF DOWNSTREAM CAUTION AT THE SAME TIME. On 10-September the Foshan spread between A00 aluminium and mixed extrusion scrap free of paint was about RMB 2,436 per tonne, and against shredded aluminium tense scrap about RMB 1,415 per tonne, both widening slightly week on week. SMM reports the scarcity of compliant, invoiced aluminium scrap continuing to rise and constraining the operating rates of scrap-consuming plants, with some yards selling actively into high prices while cutting purchases. Secondary ADC12 prices were mainly stable with slight upward adjustments in some regions on cost support from aluminium and copper.

NO NEW DATED PREMIUM ASSESSMENT PRINTED INTO THE SATURDAY COMPILE WINDOW, AND THE STANDING EVIDENCE REMAINS SOFT. The pending October-December Japanese quarterly range on this page stays at $280-310, narrowed on 11-September from $290-325 on an SMM review putting the market consensus at USD 280-290 per tonne with Korean and Thai traders already repricing toward that band, against producer offers of $310-325 opened on 02-September and a settled Q3 record of $395. The same review described premiums falling across Japan, the United States, Vietnam, South Korea and Thailand and Middle Eastern and Australian ingot supply into Japan as relatively ample. Premium assessments are periodic, so these rows are carried at their last dated public marks and nothing has been interpolated.

THE CALENDAR NARROWED TO ONE ITEM. With August payrolls, August producer prices and August consumer prices now all printed and all leaning the same way, the Federal Reserve decision next week is the largest single scheduled event on this page and the question has fully inverted from whether it cuts to whether it raises. The European Central Bank already moved, raising its three key rates 25 basis points unanimously on 10-September to a 2.50% deposit rate. TWO MAJOR CENTRAL BANKS TIGHTENING INTO THE SAME QUARTER IS A HEADWIND FOR A DOLLAR-PRICED METAL AND SIMULTANEOUSLY A BRAKE ON EVERY RESTART AND EXPANSION DECISION IN THE SUPPLY PIPELINE, so the effect on price is clearer than the effect on the physical balance.

Cash and equivalents more than doubled to USD 666.7m with no borrowings; total assets USD 2.496bn (+11.0%). THE VALUE OF THIS DISCLOSURE IS THAT IT IS A REALISED PRICE ACROSS 1.3 MILLION TONNES, NOT AN ASSESSMENT - which makes it the single best public measurement of how far alumina has actually fallen. A 39.5% decline in realised ASP to USD 320/t, against a company-stated average international alumina price of about USD 307/t on an LME Platts basis versus about USD 447/t a year earlier, confirms from the seller's own accounts that the 2024-25 alumina squeeze has fully unwound. FOR THE METAL THIS IS MARGIN-POSITIVE AND PRICE-NEGATIVE, AND BOTH LEGS DESERVE EQUAL BILLING: non-integrated smelters buy alumina cheaper, but a lower cost curve lowers the price at which supply discipline would ever appear. THE SECOND-ORDER POINT IS THE CAPITAL: cash more than doubled to USD 666.7m with no borrowings, funding preparatory work on a 250,000 t/y Indonesian electrolytic aluminium first phase at about USD 436.6m over roughly two years with a further 500,000 t/y flagged medium term. Weak alumina prices are not slowing the ex-China metal capacity pipeline - they are being converted into it. Public disclosure only; no company-specific or confidential information is used or implied.

earnings.note: Revenue RMB 11.53bn, up 32.4% year on year. Net profit attributable to owners RMB 2.30bn, up 166.1%. EPS RMB 1.11 against RMB 0.58 in the corresponding period of last year, up 91.4%. THE CLEANEST PUBLIC READ THIS WEEK ON HOW FAR SMELTER MARGIN HAS EXPANDED AT 2026 PRICES, AND IT COMES FROM AN INTEGRATED, SELF-SUPPLIED PRODUCER. The company operates 788,100 t/y of electrolytic aluminium capacity in Huolinguole, Inner Mongolia with a captive power plant, plus an alumina refining and aluminium hydroxide base in Binzhou, Shandong; it states that self-sufficiency in alumina and electricity fully meets its production requirements. Profit attributable rose 166% on revenue up 32%, which is operating leverage of roughly five times and is only possible when the price rises against a cost base that does not. Management attributes the gain to higher electrolytic aluminium selling prices, lower production cost from a rising green-energy share, and an optimised financing structure. TWO FORWARD DISCLOSURES MATTER BEYOND the quarter: 1,040 MW of wind and 110 MW of solar were commissioned by end-June with the programme roughly 66% complete and the green share expected to exceed 50%, which lowers the cost base further; and the 500,000 t/y integrated electrolytic aluminium project in Saudi Arabia, invested with partners in 2025, had completed all compliance approvals with on-site construction in full swing. earnings.note: RECORD QUARTER ACROSS EVERY SEGMENT. Consolidated revenue RS 84,825cr, up 32% year-on-year; consolidated EBITDA RS 14,989cr, up 73%; net profit RS 7,013cr, up 75%. The EBITDA margin printed 16.42% against 12.31% in Q1 FY26 and 12.82% in Q4 FY26 - a 411 basis-point expansion year-on-year and 360 basis points sequentially. INDIA ALUMINIUM UPSTREAM delivered its highest-ever quarterly EBITDA at RS 7,390cr, up 81%, comfortably exceeding the prior record of RS 5,448cr set in Q4 FY26. The COPPER segment also set a record at RS 918cr, up 36%. NOVELIS, the downstream subsidiary, reported adjusted EBITDA of $516m, up 24% from $416m a year earlier and equivalent to RS 4,875cr (+37%), with net income of $164m (+71%) and adjusted EBITDA of roughly $563 per tonne, helped by the restart of the Oswego hot mill in early June 2026 and continued Bay Minette commissioning. THIS IS THE CLEANEST PUBLIC EVIDENCE AVAILABLE OF HOW AN INTEGRATED PRODUCER CONVERTS THE 2026 PRICE STRUCTURE INTO MARGIN, AND THE CONVERSION RATE IS VERY HIGH. Revenue rose 32% while EBITDA rose 73% and upstream aluminium EBITDA rose 81% - operating leverage of well over two times on the upstream leg. The mechanism is integration: captive bauxite, captive alumina and captive coal-fired power insulate the cost stack from exactly the two legs that are currently rising for non-integrated smelters, namely seaborne bauxite (SMM index $71.57/mt, +$0.70 w/w) and seaborne alumina ($356/mt FOB East Australia on the 05-Aug trade). THE CONTRAST WITH CENTURY IS THE POINT. Century Aluminum, which buys its alumina, has now cited unfavourable raw-material price realisation as its principal EBITDA headwind for two consecutive quarters; Hindalco, which makes its own, posted a record. Management had guided to roughly 5% sequential aluminium cost inflation into this quarter and still delivered a record, which says the LME move more than absorbed it. FOR THE MARKET VIEW: this is bullish for the margin narrative and neutral-to-bearish for the supply narrative, because producers earning at this level have every incentive to run flat out and to accelerate the restart pipeline.

Constellium is a converter, not a smelter: it buys primary and scrap and sells rolled and extruded product, so a rising LME shows up in its results as a NON-CASH metal price lag benefit before it shows up anywhere in the operating business. That lag contributed $126m across the whole of FY2025 and $226m in the FIRST HALF of 2026 alone - it has nearly doubled in half the time. UNDERLYING PERFORMANCE IS GENUINELY GOOD, with ex-lag Adjusted EBITDA up 58% from $196m in Q3-2025 to $310m in Q2-2026 and the company pulling its 2028 targets forward by two years - but a reader who takes the $439m headline as operating performance overstates it by 29%. earnings.note: ADDED TO THIS PANEL THIS RUN WITH A PRIMARY-SOURCED HISTORY TAKEN DIRECTLY FROM SEC FILINGS RATHER THAN FROM COVERAGE. Kaiser reported record Q2-2026 adjusted EBITDA of $166.3m against $67.7m a year earlier, a 146% increase, on net sales of $1.2566bn and conversion revenue of $437.0m. GAAP net income was $96.8m or $5.72 per diluted share against $23.2m and $1.41. Adjusted EBITDA margin on conversion revenue doubled to 38.1% from 18.1%. H1-2026 adjusted EBITDA was $294.8m against $141.1m. Net debt leverage improved to 2.1x from 3.4x at 31-December-2025 and the full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook was raised to +45-55% year on year from +20-30%. Shipments rose 6% to 305.7 million lbs, led by packaging at 155.8 million lbs and aerospace/high-strength at 60.8 million. THE READ-THROUGH IS A WARNING ABOUT HOW MUCH OF THE 2026 DOWNSTREAM EARNINGS CYCLE IS A PRICE ARTEFACT RATHER THAN A DEMAND ONE, AND KAISER DISCLOSES IT MORE HONESTLY THAN MOST. Adjusted EBITDA includes management-estimated FAVOURABLE METAL PRICE LAG of approximately $27.0m in Q2-2026 and $36.0m in Q1-2026 - $64.0m across the half against $36.0m in H1-2025. That is roughly 22% of H1-2026 adjusted EBITDA arising from the timing difference between the Midwest Transaction Price embedded in cost of sales and the market price over the period, not from conversion economics. MANAGEMENT SAID SO EXPLICITLY: the raised full-year outlook 'assumes a NEUTRAL metal price lag through the end of the year, and does not assume a continuation of the metal lag or consumption cost tailwinds recorded in the first half', and the CEO said the company expects aluminium price dynamics to normalise over the balance of the year. THE COMMERCIAL LESSON FOR READING THIS WHOLE PANEL: a rising aluminium price inflates downstream converter earnings twice - once through genuine mix and volume, once through inventory timing - and the second half reverses if the price stops rising. Kaiser's underlying story is nevertheless real: conversion revenue per pound rose to $1.43 from $1.30, packaging conversion revenue per pound rose to $1.12 from $0.92, and aerospace shipments grew as destocking eased. Both things are true at once and the filing quantifies the split, which is why this row is worth its place.

trade.note: TRADE CORRIDORS ARE REVIEWED MONTHLY OR ON MATERIAL CHANGE RATHER THAN REFRESHED DAILY. THEY ARE RE-RATED THIS RUN AND THE TRIGGER IS SPECIFIC AND DATED: CANADA'S COUNTER-TARIFFS TAKE EFFECT TODAY, 08-SEPTEMBER-2026, AND EXPLICITLY INCLUDE ALUMINIUM. Canada is applying 15%, 25% and 50% tariffs on products drawn from those targeted by the US Section 338 and Section 232 measures, with each product's rate matched to the corresponding US rate; IN STEEL AND ALUMINIUM THE EXISTING 25% COUNTER-TARIFF RISES TO 50%. The package covers $27.6 billion of US imports and more than 300 metals products and derivatives including flat-rolled steel and aluminium bars, and is described by the Canadian government as matching the US Section 338 tariffs dollar for dollar after the US imposed 50% on $27.6 billion of Canadian goods effective 22-August. WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN A NORMAL TARIFF HEADLINE: the Canada-United States corridor is by volume the most important primary-aluminium trade route in the world, and it is now taxed in BOTH directions rather than one. THE CONSEQUENCE FOR A PHYSICAL READER IS DECOUPLING RATHER THAN SIMPLE INFLATION - regional delivered premiums on both sides of the border are mechanically supported because arbitrage between them is more expensive, while the volume that actually crosses is suppressed, so the delivered price and the exchange benchmark drift further apart. THE SECOND ACTIVE DRIVER IS UNCHANGED AND STILL UNRESOLVED: the latest escalation in US-Iran hostilities has raised uncertainty over any return of Persian Gulf supply, and Middle East LNG scarcity on tanker disruption continues to constrain regional refining and smelting.

flows.impact: Rising - and it is now the principal mechanism relieving the Western shortage
flows.note: Semi-finished exports 3.2 Mt in January-June, +18% year on year, with June at a record 695,000 t. Alloy exports nearly doubled to 238,500 t and China turned NET EXPORTER of aluminium alloy in June for the first time since 2019. Primary exports +32% to 38,400 t, much of it likely Western-origin bonded metal being redirected rather than Chinese production leaving. Driven by a tax structure that charges 30% on primary exports and zero on alloy and semis, and enabled by soft domestic demand - Citi's China end-use tracker fell 0.4% year on year while primary production rose 2.2%. The corridor consequence is that the Western physical shortage is being relieved WITHOUT unwrought metal changing hands, which is one public explanation for how a primary deficit can coexist with a flat or discounted LME front end.

flows.note: RE-RATED THIS RUN ON MATERIAL CHANGE. About 9% of global primary supply exits via the Strait of Hormuz and more than 80% of Gulf production is exported through it. THE CORRIDOR RE-ESCALATED OVER THE WEEKEND after a week in which this page had carried a de-escalation: US strikes on two Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island on 30-August, Iranian retaliation against US bases, and an IRGC claim that a supertanker caught fire after striking naval mines. Brent rose 3.19% to $90.91 on it. President Trump stated on 01-September that strikes would be limited and the Strait is 'in very good condition' with large oil volumes moving; both statements are dated and both are carried. THE PHYSICAL POSITION BEHIND THE HEADLINES IS THE PART THAT HAS NOT CHANGED: Qatalum remains at roughly 60% of its 648 kt nameplate on reduced gas with no published restart timetable and a second Hydro force majeure outstanding; Alba has reduction Lines 1, 2 and 3 idled since March, 19% of 1,623 kt, with no announced restart and a stated intention to replace rather than restart them; EGA's Al Taweelah smelter is at 25% of cells with full production reaffirmed for Q1-2027. Gulf primary output ran roughly 40% below pre-war levels in April. This is the one corridor on the page where the disruption is both real and, in Qatalum's and Alba's cases, undated.

flows.note: THE RED SEA IS DIVERGING FROM HORMUZ. Bab al Mandeb traffic fell to a weekly low of 16 commodity vessels on 26-Jul after the Houthi 'embargo' on Saudi shipping declared 20-Jul and claimed attacks on Aramco sites at Jizan and Yanbu, recovering only to 31 by 31-Jul. On 05-Aug Houthi forces claimed they had targeted a Saudi oil tanker in the Gulf of Aden and threatened further vessels in the Red Sea, with a ship reported hit the same day. A Hormuz routing agreement does not address this constraint. Saudi Arabia has been diverting crude to the Suez routing; the Suez leg for Gulf and Red Sea origin cargoes is therefore still not a clean alternative to Hormuz.

catalysts.text: THE NEXT PUBLISHED LME OFFICIAL, AND THE QUESTION HAS CHANGED NOW THAT FRIDAY'S BOARD HAS LANDED. It is no longer whether the data appears but whether the STRUCTURE holds. The 11-September session cut flat price 2.06% and left the backwardation at $24.00 against $25.00. A second and third session in which the front stays firm would confirm the sell-off was financial and unratified by the physical market; a flattening or flipping spread, or a material warehouse inflow, would say the opposite and would invalidate this page's lead finding. WATCH THE SPREAD AND THE STOCK LINE BEFORE THE FLAT PRICE.

US FEDERAL RESERVE DECISION - THE LARGEST SINGLE SCHEDULED EVENT IN FRONT OF THIS MARKET, NOW FOUR DAYS OUT. The 11-September session was the market starting to price it: core CPI a tenth above forecast, a firmer dollar, and every base metal lower together. Fed funds target is 3.50-3.75% and has been unchanged all year, and reporting describes traders raising the odds of a RISE. THE ASYMMETRY IS WORTH STATING IN ADVANCE: a hold would remove a repricing that has already been partly paid for, while a rise would extend it into a curve that has so far shifted in parallel without breaking the front.

RESOLUTION OF THE OCTOBER-DECEMBER ASIAN QUARTERLY PREMIUM. The pending range on this page is unchanged at $280-310 because no newer dated input printed - it was narrowed from $290-325 on 11-September on an SMM review putting the market consensus at USD 280-290/t with Korean and Thai traders already repricing toward that band, against producer offers of $310-325/t opened on 02-September and a settled Q3 record of $395. THE CONSENSUS SITS BELOW THE PRODUCERS' OWN OFFER FLOOR, SO THE BURDEN OF CONCESSION IS ON THE SELLERS. If it settles near $280-290 while London's curve is still backwardated, that is the strongest available evidence that physical Asia is materially looser than the exchange implies - and this run added a second, independent strand of support for that reading in SMM's statement that damaged Middle Eastern capacity has recovered.

WHETHER THE CHINESE INGOT TIGHTNESS IS STRUCTURAL OR A PRODUCT-MIX ILLUSION - THE CLEANEST GENUINELY NEW TEST ON THIS PAGE. The bullish case is precise and quantified: social inventory below 800,000 tonnes at 796,000 on 10-September; the liquid-aluminium share up to 78.93% cutting cast-ingot volume with production flat at 874,700 tonnes a week; the South China A00 basis at a year-to-date high on roughly 50,000 tonnes of genuinely tradable Foshan inventory; and at least 760,000 tonnes of new southwest molten-conversion capacity in 2026 pulled by battery-foil margins. THE FALSIFYING OBSERVATION IS ALREADY VISIBLE IN THE SAME SOURCE AND IS WATCHED RATHER THAN DISMISSED: SMM reports ALUMINIUM BILLET INVENTORY CONTINUING TO BUILD and flags it as potential pressure for inventory to shift back into ingot. If billet stock keeps building while ingot stock falls, the tightness is a mix effect that will reverse; if both fall together, it is real.

THE MONTHLY CARBON SETTLEMENT CYCLE, NOW ABOUT THREE SESSIONS AWAY. Prebaked anode and coal tar pitch settle monthly on this cadence; the September anode settlement is already public at 5,730 RMB/t spot and 5,745 RMB/t acceptance against August's 5,630, and coal tar pitch has not printed a newer mark since 13-August. SMM has guided that September anode and aluminium fluoride will both RISE. THE COST-STACK POINT IS UNCHANGED AND UNCOMFORTABLE: the comfortable reading that falling alumina means falling cash cost is not supported. Alumina's first fresh dated trade in five weeks fell only $2.50, worth about $5 a tonne of metal, while energy - the dominant line - remains materially higher across the last fortnight despite Friday's 0.78% relief in European gas.

THE MIDDLE EAST, WHERE THE QUESTION HAS QUIETLY CHANGED FROM ESCALATION TO RECOVERY. The escalation facts are unchanged and unresolved - ten ships attacked near Hormuz, five Iranian tankers sunk in retaliation, Mocha seized with leverage over Bab el-Mandeb, a naval blockade declared against Saudi Arabia - and the Iran-Oman Hormuz report remains unconfirmed with no primary announcement two days on. WHAT IS NEW IS ON THE SUPPLY SIDE AND IT POINTS THE OTHER WAY: SMM's 11-September review states that DAMAGED CAPACITY IN THE MIDDLE EAST RECOVERED and that supply outside China is repairing, the second such statement from that source in one week. AGAINST IT STAND COMPANY DISCLOSURES THAT HAVE NOT CHANGED - Qatalum at roughly 60% of nameplate with an outstanding force majeure and no resolution date, Alba's lines 1-3 idled since March. THE NEXT DATED COMPANY STATEMENT FROM EITHER OPERATOR IS WORTH MORE THAN ANY AMOUNT OF MARKET COMMENTARY AND IS THE THING TO WATCH.

THE FIRST MEASURABLE TEST OF CANADA'S COUNTER-TARIFFS, IN FORCE SINCE 08-SEPTEMBER AT 50% AGAINST A US SECTION 232 RATE OF 50% ON ARTICLES AND 25% ON DERIVATIVES. Four full days in, the only dated public evidence still points against the mechanical expectation: scattered US spot deals, lacklustre downstream consumption on the seasonal off-season, spot prices extending losses and no clear sign of stabilization. A WARNING ABOUT THE ARITHMETIC IS ISSUED IN ADVANCE RATHER THAN EXPLAINED AFTERWARDS: the US duty-paid row is carried at $2,094/t, of which $1,671.50 is the tariff leg at 50% on the $3,343.00 benchmark, leaving an implied market leg of $422.50. At a 50% rate every $10 the benchmark FALLS mechanically WIDENS the implied market leg by $5. If the next official lands near the 11-September reference level of about $3,247, the market leg will appear to widen by roughly $48 with no physical change at all.

THE EU IMPORT BAN ON RUSSIAN PRIMARY ALUMINIUM TAKES EFFECT - about fifteen weeks away. The European duty-unpaid premium is the price that must absorb it, and at a last assessment of $485/t, below its own trailing average of $519.10 and against dated commentary describing overseas premiums as broadly soft, it is not behaving as though the event is coming. Either replacement units are already sourced or the event is not priced; the assessment cadence is too slow to tell which. A MECHANISM WORTH NAMING FROM THIS RUN'S CHINESE EVIDENCE: Mysteel reports Russian cargoes in South China locked into term contracts for direct delivery to end-users. Displaced Russian metal does not float freely - it is contracted into destinations, and re-contracting it is what the remaining fifteen weeks are for. Slovalco's Q4-2026 start is two to three weeks away and is the nearest European addition standing in that squeeze.

risks.text: RE-ASSESSED 12-SEPTEMBER, SECOND COMPILE. RAISED FROM FLAT TO UP, AND THE EVIDENCE IS ARITHMETIC RATHER THAN ANECDOTAL. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS THAT TARIFF POLICY, NOT SUPPLY AND DEMAND, BECOMES THE DOMINANT DETERMINANT OF REGIONAL DELIVERED PRICE. TODAY'S PUBLISHED BOARD DEMONSTRATED THE MECHANISM DIRECTLY. Section 232 at 50% is levied on value, so the $69.00 fall in the cash benchmark cut the tariff leg of the US duty-paid price from $1,671.50 to $1,637.00 and, with the assessment unchanged at $2,094/t, MECHANICALLY WIDENED the implied market leg from $422.50 to $457.00 - an 8% apparent strengthening of the US physical premium caused by nothing physical whatsoever. WHEN A REGIONAL PREMIUM CAN MOVE 8% BECAUSE LONDON FELL TWO PERCENT, THE POLICY LEG IS DRIVING THE OBSERVED PRICE. Canada's 50% counter-tariffs, in force since 08-September, compound it. The risk is raised because the distortion is now measurable on this page rather than merely argued.

RE-ASSESSED 12-SEPTEMBER. HELD AT UP, AND IT WAS REINFORCED BY THE MOST DIRECT PIECE OF EVIDENCE THIS RISK HAS EVER RECEIVED. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS THAT CURTAILED AND DISRUPTED CAPACITY RETURNS FASTER THAN THE MARKET EXPECTS. SMM'S 11-SEPTEMBER MORNING REVIEW STATES PLAINLY THAT OUTSIDE CHINA, PRODUCTION RESUMPTIONS AND NEW CAPACITY RAMP-UPS CONTINUED, THAT DAMAGED CAPACITY IN THE MIDDLE EAST RECOVERED, AND THAT ALUMINIUM SUPPLY OUTSIDE CHINA KEPT REPAIRING. That is the second statement from the same source in one week pointing the same way, the first being that Middle Eastern and Australian ingot supply into Japan is relatively ample. ITS EVIDENTIAL WEIGHT IS DELIBERATELY CAPPED AND THE CAP IS STATED: it is market commentary, not company disclosure, and it does not override Qatalum's outstanding force majeure at roughly 60% of a 648,000-tonne nameplate or Alba's lines 1-3 idled since March 2026. NEITHER FACT HAS BEEN ADJUSTED TO FIT THE OTHER. THE SCHEDULED PIPELINE IS UNCHANGED AND ALREADY LONG: EGA at 18% guiding a return to previous output levels in early 2027; Slovalco's first 75,000 t of 175,000 guided to Q4-2026, now two to three weeks away; Alcoa's San Ciprian close to full on energy hedged through 2027 and Portland's 15,000 t completed in Q2-2026; Century's Mt Holly at full capacity for the first time since 2015; Magnitude 7 Metals' Missouri potline guided before end-2026 at ~75,000 t. THE GATING CONDITION IMPROVED ONLY FRACTIONALLY AND THE FRACTION IS NAMED: European gas gave back 0.78% to EUR 80.93, breaking a four-session run but leaving the row about 10.6% higher across five sessions, while the ECB's 25 basis point rise on 10-September raised the hurdle rate behind every restart decision in the same week.

RE-ASSESSED 12-SEPTEMBER, SECOND COMPILE. HELD AT UP AND IT HAS NOW CONVERTED FROM A FORECAST INTO A REALISED PRICE MOVE. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS THAT MACRO TIGHTENING OVERWHELMS THE PHYSICAL STORY. YESTERDAY THIS PAGE SAID THE HIGHEST-IMPACT CATALYST IT CARRIED HAD RESOLVED AGAINST THE METAL BUT COULD NOT YET SHOW IT IN A PRICE. IT CAN NOW. US August core consumer prices printed +0.3% month on month on 11-September, a tenth above forecast; the LME FX fixing moved to $1.15920 from $1.16170; and the published 11-September board carried EVERY BASE METAL LOWER - zinc -2.27%, nickel -2.06%, aluminium -2.05%, copper -0.96%, lead -0.29% on three-month officials. THAT BREADTH IS THE PROOF OF MACRO CAUSATION: five metals with unrelated fundamentals do not fall together for industrial reasons. THE FEDERAL RESERVE DECIDES ON 16-SEPTEMBER, FOUR DAYS OUT, AND THIS REMAINS THE DOMINANT RISK ON THE PAGE. THE CAVEAT IS KEPT VISIBLE: one session is not a trend, and the physical market has so far declined to ratify the move.

RE-ASSESSED 12-SEPTEMBER. HELD AT UP, BUT WITH THE STRONGEST COUNTER-EVIDENCE THIS RISK HAS FACED RECORDED IMMEDIATELY BELOW IT RATHER THAN IN A FOOTNOTE. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS GEOPOLITICAL ESCALATION AROUND GULF SUPPLY AND ITS ROUTES. NOTHING PUBLISHED IN THE 48-HOUR WINDOW CHANGED THE SITUATION IN EITHER DIRECTION AND THAT ABSENCE IS REPORTED AS AN ABSENCE, NOT AS CALM. The standing facts are unchanged: Iran said it attacked ten ships near the Strait of Hormuz and the United States said it retaliated by sinking five Iranian tankers, the worst fighting in months as the conflict nears seven months; the Houthi group was reported to have seized Mocha, gaining leverage over BAB EL-MANDEB, declaring a naval blockade against Saudi Arabia and striking Saudi energy infrastructure. TWO CONTESTED CHOKEPOINTS ARE NOT TWICE THE RISK OF ONE - THEY REMOVE THE SUBSTITUTE ROUTE. Brent is carried at $104.29 on the 11-September reference board, and its day move is deliberately NOT reported because the same board shows a positive change alongside a negative percentage on that row. THE COUNTER-EVIDENCE IS DATED, SPECIFIC AND UNCOMFORTABLE: SMM's 11-September review states that DAMAGED CAPACITY IN THE MIDDLE EAST RECOVERED and that supply outside China is repairing, alongside its earlier statement that Middle Eastern and Australian ingot supply into Japan is relatively ample. IT IS HELD AT UP RATHER THAN LOWERED FOR ONE REASON STATED EXPLICITLY: the risk as written is ESCALATION, and nothing has de-escalated in a dated, confirmed way - the Iran-Oman Hormuz report remains unconfirmed with no primary announcement two days on. But the SUPPLY-LOSS justification underneath it is now weaker than it was a week ago, and if the next dated evidence confirms Gulf recovery this risk should be lowered rather than defended.

RE-ASSESSED 12-SEPTEMBER. HELD AT FLAT ON NO NEW MARK. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS AN ALUMINA COST SHOCK PROPAGATING INTO SMELTER MARGIN. No dated alumina trade or assessment printed into a weekend compile window, so the panel is carried at its 11-September state and nothing has been interpolated. THE STANDING POSITION IS THAT THE SHOCK HAS NOT ARRIVED: 50,000 mt traded at $353.50/mt FOB EAST AUSTRALIA for October shipment on 11-September against $356/t on the IDENTICAL basis on 05-August - down $2.50, or 0.7%, over five weeks, worth about $5 a tonne of aluminium. TWO SUPPLY-SIDE FACTS STILL PULL THE OTHER WAY AND THEY ARE NOT SMALL: Alcoa cut 2026 alumina production guidance by 200,000-300,000 tonnes to 9.5-9.6 million tonnes after operational disruptions, and bauxite inventory at ten Chinese ports fell 1,610,000 tonnes in a single week. ALUNORTE REMAINS THE STRUCTURAL FRAGILITY AND THE WORD TEMPORARY REMAINS LOAD-BEARING - the world's largest alumina refinery outside China is back at full capacity on a TEMPORARY terminal-access agreement with its gas supplier, which is harder to renew in a tightening gas market than in a loosening one. THE HONEST SUMMARY IS UNCHANGED: the alumina headline is benign, the alumina supply news is not, and the cost stack overall is dominated by energy rather than by alumina.

RE-ASSESSED 12-SEPTEMBER. LOWERED FROM UP TO FLAT, AND THE REASONING IS THE MOST GENUINELY TWO-SIDED JUDGEMENT ON THIS PAGE THIS RUN. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS THAT CHINESE EXPORT SUPPLY RELIEVES THE WESTERN SHORTAGE FASTER THAN THE BALANCE FORECASTS ASSUME. THE HEADLINE EXPORT EVIDENCE IS UNCHANGED AND STILL ELEVATED: August shipments 626,000 tonnes, January-August 4.67 million tonnes, up 16.7% year on year. WHAT CHANGED IS THE PRODUCT MIX UNDERNEATH IT, AND IT CUTS BOTH WAYS AT ONCE. SMM reports Chinese weekly production HELD STEADY at 874,700 tonnes while the LIQUID-ALUMINIUM SHARE ROSE TO 78.93%, reducing cast-ingot volume; Mysteel reports Yunnan and Guangxi adding at least 760,000 tonnes of annualised molten-aluminium conversion capacity in 2026, roughly 550,000 tonnes of it Yunnan slab, and estimates FREELY TRADABLE FOSHAN INGOT INVENTORY AT ONLY ABOUT 50,000 TONNES after stripping unclear ownership, corroded warrants and Russian units locked into term contracts. THE NAIVE READING IS THAT LESS CAST INGOT MEANS LESS EXPORTABLE METAL AND THE RISK SHOULD BE LOWERED TO DOWN. THAT READING IS REJECTED HERE AND THE REJECTION IS THE POINT: the metal being diverted goes to slab and foil processors, and SEMI-FINISHED PRODUCT IS PRECISELY THE CHANNEL THROUGH WHICH CHINESE METAL ACTUALLY RELIEVES WESTERN SHORTAGE, because it does not pass through LME warehouses. THE DIVERSION MAY THEREFORE INCREASE THE RELIEVING FLOW WHILE REDUCING THE INGOT STATISTIC. Those two effects do not net to a clear direction, so the trend is set to FLAT rather than forced to a conclusion the evidence does not support.

RE-ASSESSED 12-SEPTEMBER, SECOND COMPILE. LOWERED FROM FLAT TO DOWN, AND THE TECHNICALITY THAT HELD IT AT FLAT YESTERDAY HAS BEEN REMOVED. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS THAT THE INVENTORY ARGUMENT UNDERPINNING THE BULL CASE STOPS WORKING. YESTERDAY IT WAS HELD AT FLAT ONLY BECAUSE NO WAREHOUSE LINE HAD BEEN PUBLISHED AND THE SERIES WAS FROZEN. THE LINE HAS NOW PUBLISHED AND IT WENT THE BULL CASE'S WAY: stocks drew a further 250 tonnes to 244,100, a FIFTH consecutive decline, AND IT HAPPENED ON A SESSION IN WHICH FLAT PRICE FELL 2.06%. THAT COMBINATION IS THE INFORMATIVE PART - metal did not come back to the warehouse on a sharply lower price, which is what a failing inventory argument would look like. Stocks remain roughly 7,100 tonnes below the comparison average and about 265,000 tonnes below the January peak. THE RISK IS LOWERED, NOT DISMISSED: a 250-tonne draw on a 244,000-tonne base is trivial in magnitude and a single material inflow would reverse this judgement.

RE-ASSESSED 12-SEPTEMBER, SECOND COMPILE. LOWERED FROM FLAT TO DOWN, REVERSING YESTERDAY'S DELIBERATE DOWNGRADE OF THIS PAGE'S OWN FINDING - AND THE REVERSAL IS EXPLAINED RATHER THAN QUIETLY MADE. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS THAT THE CURVE SIGNAL IS TOO SMALL OR TOO FRAGILE TO ACT ON IN EITHER DIRECTION. YESTERDAY IT WAS RAISED BECAUSE THE SIGNAL WAS FROZEN AND UNTESTED. IT HAS NOW BEEN TESTED IN THE HARSHEST AVAILABLE WAY AND IT HELD. Flat price fell 2.06% and the cash-to-three-month backwardation narrowed by ONE DOLLAR, from $25.00 to $24.00, while stocks drew again. A FRAGILE FRONT-MONTH SIGNAL DOES NOT SURVIVE A TWO-PERCENT SELL-OFF INTACT; it flattens or flips. THIS ONE DID NEITHER. Cash and three-month fell $69.00 and $68.00 - a parallel shift, which is the signature of a curve repriced by the rate path and the currency rather than by the availability of near-dated metal. THE LIMIT IS STATED PLAINLY: this is ONE session of evidence, the spread is still only $24.00, and the judgement should be re-tested on the next two or three published sessions.

RE-ASSESSED 12-SEPTEMBER. HELD AT UP. THE EU IMPORT BAN ON RUSSIAN PRIMARY ALUMINIUM TAKES EFFECT 31-DECEMBER-2026 AND IS THE LARGEST SCHEDULED STRUCTURAL EVENT ON THIS PAGE - now about fifteen weeks away. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS A DISORDERLY EUROPEAN SUPPLY RESET. THE EUROPEAN DUTY-UNPAID PREMIUM IS THE PRICE THAT MUST ABSORB IT AND IT IS STILL NOT BEHAVING AS IF THE EVENT IS COMING: last assessed at $485/t, BELOW its own trailing average of $519.10, with no newer dated mark printing into this compile window. TWO READINGS REMAIN LIVE AND THE ASSESSMENT CADENCE IS TOO SLOW TO DISTINGUISH THEM: either replacement units are already sourced and the ban is priced, or the event is not in the price at all. THE SECOND-ORDER PRESSURE EASED ONLY FRACTIONALLY AND THE FRACTION IS NAMED RATHER THAN CELEBRATED: European gas gave back about 0.78% to EUR 80.93, breaking a four-session run of gains but leaving the row roughly 10.6% higher across five sessions, while the European Central Bank raised rates 25 basis points on 10-September. THE REGION THAT MUST ABSORB A SUPPLY SHOCK AT YEAR END STILL FACES AN ELEVATED ENERGY COST AND A RISING POLICY RATE SIMULTANEOUSLY. Slovalco's Q4-2026 restart, now two to three weeks away, is the nearest European addition and sits directly in that squeeze. ONE MECHANISM WORTH NAMING FROM THIS RUN'S CHINESE EVIDENCE: Mysteel reports Russian cargoes in South China locked into term contracts for direct delivery to end-users, which is a reminder that displaced Russian metal does not float freely - it is contracted into destinations, and re-contracting it is what the fifteen weeks are for.

RE-ASSESSED 12-SEPTEMBER, SECOND COMPILE. HELD AT UP, AND TODAY SUPPLIED THE SECOND HALF OF THE PROOF. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS SOURCE-DATA INTEGRITY: that the public price source this page depends on fails to publish, publishes stale cached snapshots, or disagrees with itself. YESTERDAY THE FAILURE MODE WAS NON-PUBLICATION. TODAY IT IS SELF-DISAGREEMENT, AND IN THE OPPOSITE DIRECTION TO THE LAST TIME: the GERMAN overview carries the 11-September metals board while the ENGLISH overview still carries 10-September - the exact mirror image of the 04-August incident, when English led and German lagged. WITHIN ONE WEEK THIS SOURCE HAS EXHIBITED BOTH A PUBLICATION GAP AND A BIDIRECTIONAL LANGUAGE-VERSION DIVERGENCE. THE OPERATING RULE IS THEREFORE SETTLED AND IS NOW APPLIED ON EVERY RUN: NEITHER LANGUAGE VERSION IS RELIABLE ALONE, the newer must be established by cross-check rather than assumed from last time, and both must be reconciled against the per-metal daily tables before anything is published. The risk is held at UP because the mitigation is procedural, not structural - there is still one primary source.

balance.label: Deficit - Goldman -720 kt, Norsk Hydro -900 kt, Macquarie -930 kt; Citi an outlier at -2.7 Mt. THE BALANCE VIEW IS UNCHANGED AND THE 11-SEPTEMBER DATA SHARPENS THE CENTRAL PUZZLE RATHER THAN RESOLVING IT: global primary production was reported down 1.7% year on year at 6.16 million tonnes and GCC output down 44% year on year in July to 293,000 tonnes from 523,000 - a genuine, large supply loss. YET China's August exports were 626,000 tonnes, taking January-August to 4.67 million tonnes, up 16.7% year on year, and dated commentary describes Middle Eastern and Australian ingot supply into Japan as RELATIVELY AMPLE with Asian premiums collapsing toward a $280-290 Q4 consensus. A DEFICIT IN PRIMARY UNITS CAN COEXIST WITH AMPLE REGIONAL AVAILABILITY IF THE RELIEVING METAL ARRIVES AS CHINESE SEMI-FINISHED AND ALLOY PRODUCT THAT NEVER PASSES THROUGH AN LME WAREHOUSE - which is the most coherent published explanation for why a multi-decade exchange inventory low, a widening backwardation and collapsing physical premiums are all true at once.

The published restart schedule is the reason, and it gained another dated entry on 20-August. Nanshan Aluminum's 2026 semi-annual report confirms 250,000 t/y of Indonesian aluminium and 260,000 t/y of carbon under construction at Bintan Industrial Park, with the integrated anode carbon removing one of the genuine physical constraints on commissioning new non-Chinese capacity. Alongside it: Gulf pre-incident output guided for Q1-2027 and running faster than the market expected; Slovalco 75,000 t/y from Q4-2026; Magnitude 7 Metals 75,000 t/y before year-end; Mount Holly already at full capacity and lifting US primary output by close to 10%; the Australian smelter's power secured to 2038 removing a closure risk over up to 590,000 t/y; Alunorte back at full rate; and a 500,000 t/y integrated Saudi greenfield through all compliance approvals with construction under way. These are published commitments with dates attached rather than projections, which is why the deficit is expected to narrow rather than persist at 2026 scale.

caveats: THE 11-SEPTEMBER LME BOARD IS PUBLISHED AND IS THE BASIS OF EVERY EXCHANGE FIGURE ON THIS PAGE - cash, three-month, spread, stock, the five-metal board, the per-metal detail, the fifteen-session price and stock series and the fifteen-session per-metal cash series. It was taken from Westmetall's GERMAN overview requested with a cache-busting query string and confirmed line for line against the aluminium, copper and zinc per-metal daily tables. THE ENGLISH OVERVIEW STILL CARRIES 10-SEPTEMBER AND WAS NOT USED FOR THE METALS BOARD.

THIS IS THE MIRROR IMAGE OF THE 04-AUGUST CACHE INCIDENT, WHEN THE ENGLISH PAGE LED AND THE GERMAN PAGE LAGGED. The operating rule is therefore confirmed in both directions: neither language version of this source is reliable on its own and the newer of the two must be established by cross-check on every run.

THIS IS THE SECOND COMPILE PUBLISHED ON 12-SEPTEMBER. The earlier one correctly carried the 10-September official because Friday's board had not yet been posted. This run supersedes it on the exchange figures only; the premium, alumina, input-basket, producer-status, peer-earnings and outlook research from that run stands and is unchanged except where the new benchmark changes an arithmetic result.

THE ENTIRE BASE-METALS BOARD FELL ON THE SAME SESSION, so no row on this page should be read as a metal-specific signal without that context. On three-month officials: zinc -2.27%, nickel -2.06%, aluminium -2.05%, copper -0.96%, lead -0.29%.

THE ATTRIBUTION OF THE FALL TO THE US AUGUST CPI PRINT AND A FIRMER DOLLAR IS A STRONG INFERENCE, NOT A CONFIRMED CAUSAL FACT. What is confirmed and dated is the print itself (11-September, core +0.3% month on month against +0.2% expected), the FX fixing move to $1.15920 from $1.16170, and the simultaneous fall across all five metals. The causal link between them is reasoning from coincidence of timing and breadth, and it is labelled as such.

ONE SESSION IS NOT A TREND. The claim that the physical market has not ratified the paper move rests on a single day of a held backwardation and a 250-tonne stock draw. Both are small. The claim should be re-tested on the next two or three published sessions and would be invalidated by a flattening front or a material warehouse inflow.

PREMIUM ASSESSMENTS ARE PERIODIC AND ARE CARRIED AT THEIR LAST PUBLIC ASSESSMENT DATE; they have not been advanced to 11-September. The US tariff-versus-market decomposition, by contrast, IS recomputed every run because its tariff leg is a fixed percentage of the current benchmark.

THE INPUT BASKET IS LARGELY UNCHANGED. Only the copper row moved, because it is the only input on the basket with a daily public exchange mark; its fifteen-session history rolled onto 11-September with the LME board. No monthly carbon settlement, weekly fluoride-salt mark or new silicon or magnesium quotation printed into this window, and no history has been interpolated to fill a gap.
NO PEER RESULTS WERE REPORTED IN THE WINDOW. The peer-earnings table and the per-company earnings-history series are unchanged and remain PUBLIC LISTED-COMPANY INFORMATION ONLY.

EVERYTHING PUBLISHED HERE IS PUBLIC, SOURCED AND GENERIC MARKET INFORMATION. No confidential, internal or company-specific data appears on this page. The only company references are public listed-company disclosures in the peer-earnings and producer-status panels.
